title: How do we remove brackets and keep the same value?
description: Six expressions with brackets are written without brackets, using the rule that a plus keeps the signs and a minus flips them. Each result is checked by comparing values.
teaching_notes: Let the child try first, then compare. One idea: look at the sign before each bracket. Ask the child to check each new expression against working the bracket first.

video_script.why: The child removes brackets from six expressions by looking at the sign before each bracket, as in the shop example.
video_script.substitution: The same rule works with other numbers: look at the sign before the bracket, then keep or flip the signs inside.
video_script.payoff_line: Look at the sign before each bracket, then keep or flip the signs inside.

final_answer.spoken: fourteen plus twelve plus ten, fourteen minus twelve minus ten, fourteen plus twelve minus ten, fourteen minus twelve plus ten, minus fourteen plus twelve minus ten, and fourteen plus twelve plus ten

video_script.design: One idea: look at the sign before each bracket, then keep or flip the signs inside. The six expressions stay in the anchor band; the working band shows each removal. No hard clear.
open_questions: The book text shows the fifth expression as minus 14 plus 12 minus 10 with no bracket, while the worklist question has a bracket round 12 minus 10. The video follows the worklist.
